# Change trajectory evidence without weakening replay checks

## Context
Load conventions. [`validate()`](mex://function:b081c62f402aaf28c06d252cf11bc392) defines strict record shapes; replay [`main()`](mex://function:1b12ff5eb99a0a1c5775d4909e4dfca9) validates baselines before comparison. Sources: `scripts/nightshift-trajectory.py:42`, `evals/trajectory/replay.py:16`.

## Steps
1. Identify the status, route, or policy record branch being changed in `scripts/nightshift-trajectory.py:47`.
2. Update exact keys and permitted values together; extend validation cases for unknown fields and invalid types (`scripts/nightshift-trajectory.py:49`).
3. Review expected evidence in `evals/trajectory/baseline.json` before changing it; the replay loads that file by default (`evals/trajectory/replay.py:18`).

## Gotchas
Replay rejects duplicate baseline keys and requires the scenario set to match exactly. It compares complete actual and expected records. Source: `evals/trajectory/replay.py:22`.

## Verify
- [ ] Run `python3 evals/trajectory/replay.py`; require every scenario to report matching. Source: `evals/trajectory/replay.py:36`.
- [ ] Exercise unknown fields, invalid enum values, and malformed attempt records. Source: `scripts/nightshift-trajectory.py:44`.

## Debug
An invalid-baseline error precedes recording. A mismatch can reflect a recording exception or unequal evidence; inspect that scenario instead of replacing the baseline wholesale. Source: `evals/trajectory/replay.py:32`.

## Update Scaffold
- [ ] Update `.mex/ROUTER.md` if project state changed.
- [ ] Update affected `.mex/context/` files and grounding after behavior changes.
- [ ] Update `.mex/patterns/INDEX.md` when adding a task pattern.
